note: CODE DERIVATION: the processing script renames deposit columns PWIk_covid (T1), M2_PWIk_post (T2), M3_PWIk_post (T3) to PWIk and keeps PWIk_pre as-is -- number-preserving renames, no positional step. NO LABELS: both deposits are ';'-delimited CSVs with bare headers. MAPPING: paper_explicit -- the 2021 supplementary .docx (Supp. Table note) says 'PWI-A1 to PWI-A8 = difference scores between the reports on the individual PWI-A items (respectively, general life satisfaction, standard of living, health, achieving in life, relationships, safety, community connectedness and future security)', and the 2023 ReadThisFirst.txt says the PWI totals are computed 'without PWI_1, a general life satisfaction item'. So PWI1 = the optional life-as-a-whole item and PWI2..PWI8 = PWI core domains 1..7 in manual order. Verified against the data (verify_depue_2023_pwi.R, VERIFIED: all 64 published M/SD in 2023 Table 3 reproduced within 0.005). _pre vs current: ReadThisFirst: 'The PWI-A was administered twice: once focused on the period before COVID-19 (indicated by _pre) and once focused on the past month' -- the _pre ratings were asked retrospectively at T1 only. The study's own framing for those two reference periods is not published anywhere in the deposit or papers, so PWIk and PWIk_pre ship the same stem and the difference is stated in public_note only (no invented section_prompt). LANGUAGE: 'The language of the survey was Dutch' (2021 paper, Methods); 'the Dutch version of the Personal Wellbeing Index-Adults' (both papers). No Dutch PWI wording is in either OSF deposit (two CSVs, two ReadThisFirst.txt), either supplementary .docx, or either PMC full text -- so translated_substitute fallback: the manual's English ships in the base fields with language=Dutch and no _translated columns. TEXT: stems, instructions and anchors transcribed from the manual's written format (Section 4). Deviations: surrounding quotation marks on the stems dropped; a stray unmatched closing quote after the 4.1 instruction sentence dropped; the manual's space before '?' ('...your health ?') kept as printed. Anchors 'No satisfaction at all' (0) and 'Completely Satisfied' (10) as printed (the manual breaks them over lines); resp 1-9 are unlabelled in the instrument, so option_text is blank there. The papers state the same anchors ('no satisfaction at all' = 0, 'completely satisfied' = 10). RESP: deposit stores x10 (0-100); the script divides by 10 so live resp is the administered 0-10 point; no reverse keying in the PWI. RIGHTS: no instrument_rights_register.csv row for the PWI. The originator's manual (front matter, 1.4-1.7) and the ACQOL instruments page carry no copyright, permission, fee, non-commercial or redistribution clause -- only a citation request ('Citation of Reference for this Scale: International Wellbeing Group (2013)...'). Silence = permission under the irw#1945 test, so extracted normally. Caveat: the live ACQOL page could not be read (Deakin bot challenge), only its 2021 Wayback capture. No register row written (a round may not write ship). COUNTS: 16 items x 11 = 176 rows; live PWIk: 640 (T1) + 371 + 371, PWI5/PWI5_pre 639 at T1 (one deposit row blank on both PWI5 columns; the 2021 paper's Table 2 counts 213/398/29 = 640 for relationships vs 212/398/29 live -- a one-case difference in the paper's count, not an IRW defect).
public_note: Respondents answered the Dutch version of the PWI-A but the item text shown is the International Wellbeing Group's English; items PWI1-PWI8 were rated for the past month (at each of three waves), while PWI1_pre-PWI8_pre are the same questions rated retrospectively, at the first wave, for the period before COVID-19 -- the study's own wording for those two reference periods is not published.
